title: Kitchen Renovation Cost Average: UK Guide
description: Kitchen renovation cost average explained by project scope, materials, labour and extras, with practical UK budgeting guidance for homeowners planning a refit.

blocks.text: If you are searching for the average cost of a kitchen renovation in the UK, there is no single price. A small cosmetic refresh can cost a few thousand pounds, while a full renovation involving new units, flooring, plumbing, electrics and structural changes can run into tens of thousands. As a rough guide, a professionally fitted kitchen renovation may typically cost between £8,000 and £25,000, although the size of the room, specification, location and amount of preparation required can move the figure considerably. Every project differs, so use these figures only for early planning and get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
Average kitchen renovation cost by project scope

The most useful way to estimate your budget is to define the level of work required. A renovation that keeps the existing layout and services may cost less than one that changes the position of the sink, cooker or appliances. Labour availability, access to the property and the condition of the existing room can also affect the final price.

items: Cosmetic refresh: as a rough guide, typically £3,000 to £8,000. This may include repainting, replacing handles, updating worktops, fitting a new splashback, changing lighting or replacing selected appliances while keeping the existing cabinets and layout.

Partial kitchen renovation: as a rough guide, typically £8,000 to £15,000. This may include new cabinet doors or cabinets, worktops, flooring, tiling and appliance upgrades, with limited changes to plumbing and electrics.

Standard full renovation: as a rough guide, typically £15,000 to £25,000. This may cover units, worktops, appliances, flooring, decoration, plumbing, electrical work and installation, depending on the chosen materials and the work required.

Higher-specification or complex renovation: typically £25,000 and upwards. Bespoke cabinetry, premium appliances, stone worktops, extensive electrical work, structural alterations or an open-plan redesign can increase the cost. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

What materials do to the overall budget

Cabinetry can be one of the larger parts of a kitchen budget. Flat-pack units may reduce the initial material cost, while rigid, made-to-measure or bespoke cabinetry can cost more. The right choice depends on the shape of the room, the storage you need and how much adjustment is required during fitting. Replacing only doors and drawer fronts may be a way to change the appearance where the existing cabinet carcasses are sound.

Worktop material can make a noticeable difference to the budget. Laminate is often a lower-cost option, while solid timber, compact laminate, quartz and other stone surfaces can cost more depending on thickness, edge details, templating and installation. Appliance costs also vary widely: a basic oven, hob and extractor package may cost less than premium integrated appliances, an American-style fridge-freezer or specialist cooking equipment.

items: Cabinet doors, drawer fronts and handles: cost depends on whether you are refreshing existing units or replacing the full carcasses.
Worktops: allow for the material, joins, cut-outs, edging and fitting, not just the price per metre.
Appliances: compare the purchase price with delivery, installation, connection and disposal of the old appliance.
Flooring: vinyl and laminate may be lower-cost choices, while porcelain tiles, natural stone and complex patterns can add material and labour costs.
Splashbacks and wall tiling: budget for adhesive, grout, trims, preparation and any removal of existing finishes.

blocks.text: How much of the cost is labour?

Labour is not simply a charge for assembling cabinets. A kitchen renovation may involve removing the old kitchen, protecting the property, preparing walls and floors, fitting units, levelling worktops, connecting plumbing, completing electrical work, installing appliances, tiling and decorating. Labour and installation costs depend on the scope of work, preparation required, access, the number of trades involved and the complexity of the design. A simple replacement with no layout changes may need less labour than a renovation requiring multiple trades and extensive preparation.

Common extras that can push up a kitchen budget

The quoted price for units and fitting may not be the complete cost of a renovation. Existing conditions can become clearer when the old kitchen is removed, so it can be sensible to keep a contingency rather than allocating the entire budget to finishes. The appropriate contingency depends on the age and condition of the property, the amount of alteration planned and the level of uncertainty in the initial survey.

items: Removal and disposal of the old kitchen, including cabinets, worktops, flooring and redundant appliances.
Moving water, waste, gas or electrical points to suit a new layout.
Electrical upgrades, additional sockets or improved task and under-cabinet lighting.
Floor levelling, damp repairs, plastering or making good after old units and tiles are removed.
Structural work, such as removing a wall or installing support, where an open-plan layout is proposed.
Building work outside the kitchen, including pipework alterations, ventilation or changes to doors and windows.
Delivery charges, parking, difficult access, temporary storage and the cost of supplying or installing appliances.

blocks.text: Practical ways to control your renovation cost

Start with a written brief that separates essentials from upgrades. Decide whether the layout must change, which appliances need replacing and whether you want a complete refit or a visual update. Keeping plumbing and electrical points in their current positions can reduce disruption, although it should not override a poor layout or safety requirement. Obtain itemised quotations that show units, worktops, appliances, preparation, labour, waste removal and any provisional sums.

Choose finishes in order of priority rather than trying to make every element premium. For example, you might invest in durable worktops and reliable appliances while selecting simpler handles or splashback tiles. Confirm measurements before ordering, check appliance dimensions carefully and allow time for lead times. A free, no-obligation quote can help turn an initial range into a project-specific budget. faq.q: What is the average cost of a kitchen renovation in the UK?
faq.a: As a rough guide, a professionally fitted kitchen renovation may typically cost around £8,000 to £25,000. Smaller cosmetic updates can cost less, while bespoke finishes, layout changes and structural work can take the total above £25,000. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: What is the cheapest way to renovate a kitchen?
faq.a: Keeping the existing layout, retaining sound cabinets, replacing doors and handles, and choosing budget-friendly worktops and flooring may reduce costs. Check the condition of the underlying units and services before deciding what to retain.

faq.q: How much should I budget for kitchen fitting labour?
faq.a: There is no reliable single percentage for kitchen fitting labour. The amount depends on the room, preparation, access, number of trades, materials and whether plumbing or electrics need moving. An itemised, project-specific quote is the best way to budget accurately.

faq.q: What is usually included in a full kitchen renovation?
faq.a: A full renovation may include removal, preparation, cabinets, worktops, appliances, plumbing, electrical work, flooring, tiling, decorating and installation. Check each quotation carefully because inclusions vary between contractors.

faq.q: Should I keep a contingency for a kitchen renovation?
faq.a: It can be sensible to keep a contingency for unexpected work, especially in older properties or where finishes are being removed. Hidden damage, uneven floors, outdated wiring and changes made during the project can affect the final cost.
